newsitem.title: USA: Chemical firms to pay $25 million in fines - U.S.
newsitem.headline: Chemical firms to pay $25 million in fines - U.S.

text.p: Chemical companies Hoffmann-La Roche and Jungbunzlauer International AG have agreed to pay $25 million in criminal fines for fixing the price of citric acid worldwide, the Justice Department announced Wednesday.

The Justice Department said its latest catches in the international criminal conspiracy will bring its recovery in fines to more than $195 million. Those fines included $50 million, which a subsidiary of Bayer Co. agreed to in January, and $100 million which Archer Daniels Midland Co. agreed to in October.
In the latest case, Hoffmann-La Roche has agreed to pay $14 million and Jungbunzlauer $11 million and the companies will cooperate in investigations. Company officials also have agreed to fines.

Udo Haas, former managing director of SA Citrique Belge NV, which produces citric acid for Hoffmann-La Roche, and Rainer Bichlbauer, chairman and president of Jungbunzlauer, have agreed to plead guilty and each pay a $150,000 criminal fine.

The pleas are contingent on approval by a Federal District Court judge in San Francisco. But even before the approval, which was expected, a key Justice Department official promised the investigation would continue.

"The department will continue to seek out and prosecute all international conspiracies that increase prices for consumers and unfairly impede free and open competition in our markets," said Joel Klein, acting assistant attorney general of the antitrust division.
